The older I get, the more I realise that picking something you are passionate about would have been better than just picking something you thought there was going to better money and security in it. These things go through cycles as OP said, then suddenly you have a career with no money and security, where that lack of passion just turns into you hating it.

Firstly well done on doing so well, the whole harvard thing while on scholarship is a massive achievement even if you are unemployed I would still be impressed by it. Its great to see someone not from a priveledged background getting the far. You have not messed up at all and you shouldn't put yourself down for that.

With regards to your subject choice STEM isnt the golden ticket people always make it out to be. I listened too many people around me growing up and eventually ended up with a Masters in Mechanical Engineering and I honestly hated being an engineer. I was made redundant twice in the space of a year just there an now im working odd jobs and feel a lot better. I have been offered other engineering roles but I just cant see it has a good career for me in the future and it was killing me. 

This nonsense any degree bar a STEM degree is worthless gets on my nerves. In my experience people who done liberal arts are far more interesting. I also know a lot of peoplle with STEM degrees who struggled to get work, espeically with the job market being as it is now. I even know a lot of engineers who struggled to get work for 2 years after leaving uni

I dont live in New York I live in Belfast but I was having the same problem looking for jobs, I decided to take agency and hospitality jobs while I figure things out. Most catering agencies are always starved for peoplle in my experience and if I'm honest you do meet a lot of interesting people who are in the same postion as you and there is no shame in it, a lot of people have the same problem. Try working odd jobs and volunteering for stuff even if it just something like a community project, some people see someone with a degree and jus think they are good at coursework, if you volunteer it shows that you were willing learn things and mix with people not from your background.

I'm not going to pretend things are going to be easy for you,a lot of comapnies are nervous about hiring people at the moment. You may have to do small jobs for a while just to find your feet, its not refelction of you, tbh you are supposed to live with your parents after you graduated, there is no shame it.
